title: CrealityPrint is now installable from a Flatpak repository (FlatPark)
originalText:
Hi @hemiao2023 — thanks for CrealityPrint. I maintain **FlatPark**, a small hub that offers Flatpak installs for apps that aren't on Flathub, and I've packaged CrealityPrint there, in response to #472.
It uses Flatpak **extra-data**, so it downloads your **official `CrealityPrint-V -x86_64-Release.AppImage`** from your GitHub releases unmodified at install time and tracks new releases automatically — I don't rehost or patch anything. The AppImage is unpacked offline at install time, so no FUSE is needed.
Install:
App page:
Packaging notes, in case they're useful:
- App id: `io.github.crealityofficial.CrealityPrint`, the same one as your in-tree Flatpak manifest, so it's the same application. It runs on GNOME 51. The launcher sets the AppImage's own library path plus the two settings from your `flatpak/entrypoint` (`LC_ALL=C.UTF-8`, and the WebKit DMA-BUF switch on NVIDIA).
- Permissions follow your manifest's `finish-args`: network, `--device=all`, the home directory, removable media, the spacenav socket and UDisks2.
- Two libraries come from outside the AppImage: `libdeflate.so.0` from Debian, and a `libbz2.so.1.0` link to the runtime's `libbz2.so.1`. …

title: Source code for cr_FillTensor and cr_tpms (AGPL-3.0 section 6)
originalText:
CrealityPrint is based on OrcaSlicer and licensed under AGPL-3.0. Your release builds link two libraries whose source isn't in this repo:
- `deps/CR_CLOSED/CR_FILLTENSOR` (cr_FillTensor_library), called from `src/libslic3r/Fill/FillField.cpp` and `PrintObject.cpp` for Adaptive TPMS
- `deps/CR_TPMS` (cr_tpms_library), called from `src/libslic3r/Fill/FillTpmsGradual.cpp` for Gradual TPMS
Only headers and prebuilt .lib/.a/.dll files are in the repo. According to the FillTensor README, they're built by an internal Jenkins job (CR_Close_library build #6, source revision a2b46ff4278bca9f6eb1c0862ac48cf5d1775a2a). That job runs at a private network address, 172.20.180.14.
Both are linked into libslic3r and called directly by the slicer, so they're part of the Corresponding Source as section 1 defines it. Under section 6 that source has to be available to anyone who receives the object code. I downloaded V7.3.0 from your GitHub releases.
Please publish the source of both libraries at the revisions in V7.3.0, including their build scripts, under AGPL-3.0. Here in the repo or anywhere public is fine.
Related: #340

title: K2: print paused over 1 h (e.g. filament runout) cannot be resumed - idle_timeout M84 drops Z, RESUME purges then fails "Must home axis first", retry heats to 0 [fw 1.1.6.7.2]
originalText:
【Summary】
If a print stays paused for more than an hour (typically a filament runout overnight), it can no longer be resumed. `idle_timeout` runs its default `TURN_OFF_HEATERS` + `M84` while the job is paused. `M84` clears Z homing, and nothing can re-home Z safely with a part on the bed. When the user then presses Resume, the printer reheats, homes X/Y, purges about 82 mm at the purge position, and then aborts with `Must home axis first` before it returns to the part. The job stays paused.
A second Resume makes it worse. The first attempt already set `PRINTER_PARAM.hotend_temp` to 0, so `RESUME_EXTERNAL` now runs `M109 S0` / `M104 S0` and tries to push the 82 mm purge through a cold nozzle. From the user's side, the printer "turns the heaters off and tries to extrude".
【Environment】
- Printer: K2, hw `CR0CN200400C10`
- System firmware: `1.1.6.7.2`
- Stock `printer.cfg`: `[idle_timeout] timeout: 3600`, no `gcode:` option, so Klipper's default `TURN_OFF_HEATERS` / `M84` applies
- Stock `gcode_macro.cfg` PAUSE / RESUME / RESUME_EXTERNAL chain
【Reproduction (seen on a real 22 h TPU job)】
1. Filament runs out, `filament_switch_sensor` pauses the job (`key358`). …

title: GPL v3 source and config request: Ender-3 V3, Ender-3 V3 Plus, Ender-5 Max, K2 SE
originalText:
Creality's product pages say these printers run "Open-source Creality OS Based on Klipper", and the firmware download pages distribute their OTA images as password-protected archives:
- Ender-3 V3 (the F001 images on its firmware page)
- Ender-3 V3 Plus (F001_ota_img_V1.2.3.8.img on its firmware page)
- Ender-5 Max (F004_ota_img_V1.2.0.09.img and V1.2.0.10)
- K2 SE (CR4CU220812S11_ota_img_V2.3.6.43.img and V2.3.6.49)
Klipper is licensed under the GNU GPL v3. Distributing a Klipper-based firmware binary carries the obligation to make the corresponding source available to its recipients, and the machine configuration (printer.cfg and the config directory) is what lets third-party software home and park these machines the way the firmware expects. This organization already publishes Klipper repositories for the K1 series, the K2 series, the Hi, the Ender-3 V3 KE and the CR-10 SE; nothing is published for these four.
Could you publish the source and the config directory for these four machines the same way, or add them to the existing repositories? I sent the same request to cs@ on 2026-09-17.

title: Optimize color change time
originalText:
【Is your feature request related to a problem?】
I think we found a significant source of unnecessary delay during filament/color changes on the Creality K2/CFS.
The issue does not appear to be the mechanical speed of the CFS itself, but rather **the order in which the firmware handles nozzle temperature during a filament change**.
【What is happening now】
During a color change, the toolhead moves to the left side near the filament cutter and spends several seconds there before the cut is actually performed. On my machine, this alone is roughly a 10-second window.
However, instead of using this time to start heating the nozzle toward the purge temperature, the printer performs most of the mechanical filament-change process first:
cut → retract old filament → CFS movement → load new filament → temperature management → purge.
In practice, the nozzle can remain at, or even be returned toward, a lower temperature during these operations. Only later does the machine heat to the normal extrusion temperature and then finally raise the target again to the higher purge temperature. …

The `master-server` service crashes with a segmentation fault (`SIGSEGV`, signal 11) and enters an infinite crash-loop when a gcode file on the printer contains 17 filament entries in its metadata and at least one of those entries is mapped to the external spool holder. This renders the touchscreen, Creality Print LAN control, and Creality Cloud mobile app completely non-functional. The only recovery is to delete the offending gcode file.
【Background】
The K2 Plus supports two filament sources:
- **CFS (Continuous Filament System):** 4 boxes × 4 slots = 16 slots
- **External spool holder:** 1 slot
The printer's own internal configuration (`box_config.json`) stores all 17 filament entries (T1–T4 boxes + `rackMaterial`).
